scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

The situation is that the person lied to make their boyfriend feel better and to help him move on faster. They're both college seniors, and they've only been dating for four months. The boyfriend had been dating another girl for his first two years in college, and they broke up because he suspected she was cheating based on rumors from a party. The person who is lying had a crush on the boyfriend since freshman year but knew he was in a relationship. At the party in question, the ex-girlfriend was rumored to have danced and kissed another guy. The person who is lying was also at the party but doesn't remember seeing the ex-girlfriend because it was a huge event with many people, and they didn't have overlapping friend circles. When the boyfriend asked if they had seen his ex at the party, they lied and said they had seen her with other guys. This seemed to help the boyfriend move on faster and feel better about the breakup, as he now felt certain that his ex had cheated on him. The person is now feeling guilty about lying and wants to know if they're "the asshole" for lying and keeping up the lie. They acknowledge that telling the truth now wouldn't gain them anything, and the boyfriend is happier now without regrets about his ex. So, is lying in this situation right or wrong? Let's break it down. First, lying can have serious consequences. Trust is a fundamental aspect of any relationship, and lying can erode that trust. If the boyfriend found out about the lie, it could damage the relationship severely. On the other hand, the person lied with the intention of helping their boyfriend feel better and move on. They wanted to give him closure and reduce his emotional pain. It's also important to consider the context. The boyfriend was still emotionally tied to his ex, and the breakup was causing him distress. The person wanted to support him and provide him with a reason to feel better about the breakup. By lying, they gave him a clear answer that justified the breakup and helped him move on faster. However, lying, even with good intentions, can still be harmful. It undermines honesty, which is crucial in a healthy relationship. The person might feel guilty or anxious about keeping the lie alive, which can create internal conflict and stress. Another angle to consider is the potential long-term effects. If the lie is never discovered, it might not cause immediate harm, but it sets a precedent for dishonesty in the relationship. This could lead to issues down the line if similar situations arise, and trust becomes harder to maintain. Additionally, the boyfriend's happiness and emotional well-being are important. If the lie helped him feel better and move on, it could be seen as a positive action in the short term. However, it's also possible that the boyfriend might have dealt with his emotions in a healthier way if he had the truth, even if it was harder to accept. In summary, while the intention behind the lie was to help the boyfriend, lying itself is generally considered wrong because it violates trust and honesty, which are essential in any relationship. The short-term benefits of the lie might have helped the boyfriend feel better, but the long-term consequences could be damaging to the relationship's foundation. Therefore, it's likely that lying in this situation is wrong, despite the good intentions behind it.
